stem: Packets of Frugums contain 30 sweets. The manufacturer claims that, on average, 17% of the sweets are orange flavoured. Angela suspects that the average is actually less than 17%. In order to test the manufacturer’s claim, she buys a packet of Frugums. If there are fewer than 3 orange flavoured sweets in the packet, she will conclude that the claim is false.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: State appropriate null and alternative hypotheses.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by a Type I error in this situation.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: Calculate the probability of a Type I error.

parts.label: (iv)
parts.text: Given that the true percentage of orange flavoured sweets is 5%, calculate the probability of a Type II error.
